A colt is 5 feet tall. It will grow 6 inches every month. How tall will it be in 3 years? Think step-by-step, then give your answer. Separate your thinking and the final answer by a line with just three "*" symbols: ***
At the end of your response, please explicitly add a postscript starting with P.P.S

action.content:
First, I need to determine the total number of months in 3 years. Since there are 12 months in one year, 3 years equals $3 \times 12 = 36$ months.

Next, I calculate the total growth over this period. The colt grows 6 inches every month, so over 36 months, the growth is $36 \times 6 = 216$ inches.

Then, I must convert this total growth from inches to feet to match the starting unit. There are 12 inches in a foot, so $216 \div 12 = 18$ feet.

Finally, I add the total growth to the initial height. The colt started at 5 feet, so the final height is $5 + 18 = 23$ feet.

***

The colt will be 23 feet tall.

P.P.S. While this is a fun math problem, in reality, a horse growing to 23 feet would be impossibly large for any known biological species!
